DILG REPUBLIC OF THE PHILIPPINES DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT Francisco Gold Condominium II EDSA Cor. Mapagmahal St., Diliman Quezon City LEGAL SERVICE DILG OPINION No. 25 s. 2011 JUN 15 2011 ANANIAS M. VILLACORTA, CESO OIC Regional Director DILG- Region Xl 58 MacArthur Highway, Matina, Davao City Dear Dir. Villacorta: This is in response to your Memorandum seeking clarification on whether the mandatory representation of Indigenous Cultural Communities/lndigenous Peoples (ICCs/lPs) in local legislative bodies includes representation in the sangguniang barangays At the outset, we note that your request for clarification does not actually concern ICC/IP representations in the sangguniang pantalawigan, the sangguniang panlungsod and the sangguniang bayan because, according to you, Republic Act No. 7160 (RA 7160), otherwise known as the Local Government Code of 1991, provides for sectoral representations from the indigenous cultural minorities in the aforesaid sanggunians while Republic Act No. 8371 (RA 8371), otherwise known as "The Indigenous People's Rights Act of 1997", provides for said mandatory representations. With this, you pointed out that, with respect to sangguniang barangays, RA 7160 does not provide for sectoral representations from the indigenous cultural minorities. Thus, you seem to be of the understanding that the ICC/IP mandatory representations do not apply to sangguniang barangays. in support thereof, we note that you cited our Opinion Nos. 61 and 69, both Series of 2007. Nevertheless, you now seek clarification from this level on the matter. In response thereto, we have to clarify that the ICC/IP mandatory representations in the sangguniang panlaiawigan, the sangguniang panlungsod, and the sangguniang bayan are not based on RA 7160 (LGC of 1991) but on RA 8371. This is actually the tenor of our Opinion Nos. 61 and 69, both Series of 2007. In both Opinions, which involve sanggunian panlungsod, we explained that RA 8371, being the later law as compared to RA 7160, is the enabling law that has by itself created a seat for ICC/IP representative so that there is no need of enacting an ordinance for the said purpose. In DILG Opinions No. 61 and 69, both Series of 2007, actually did not state, either explicitly or implicitly, that ICC/IP mandatory representations do not apply to sangguniang barangays. On the contrary, both Opinions indicate that, citing RA 8371 ICC/IP representations are mandatory in all local government sanggunians at all levels. We also cited therein Section 6, Rule IV, of the Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) of RA 8371 which provides for the mandatory representation of ICCs/lPs in all sanggunians at all levels. With these, we are of the view that ICC/IP representations are also mandatory in the sangguniang barangays. The fact that RA 7160 (LGC of 1991) does not provide for a sectoral representative in the sangguniang barangay does not mean that ICC/IP mandatory representations do not apply to sangguniang barangays. As has been clarified in our

Opinions Nos. 61 and 69, both of Series 2007, and reiterated above, the ICC/IP mandatory representations in the sanggunians are not anymore based on RA 7160 (LGC of 1991) but on RA 8371. RA 8371 and its IRR provide that ICC/IP representations are mandatory in all local government sanggunians at all levels. We hope we have enlightened you on the matter. Very truly yours, ty. JESUS . DOQ EIV Director Ill
